text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime minister speaks on plans for social sector, promises a new Nationalist Party government will support voluntary organisations.
- Democratic Alternative, a tiny political group standing for the October 26 elections, calls for legisation to regulate donations to political parties.
- Hopes for tourism upturn rising. British tourism audit firm sees rise in bookings for winter tourism in Malta.

- Opposition Labour Party leader Alfred Sant says Labour government will not touch the retirement age. The ruling Nationalist government wants Malta to join the European Union but Sant said that included the risk that the retirement age, currently at 61, would be increased in line with other European countries.
- Electoral Commission receives first nominations for October 26 poll.
- Prime minister says peace of mind was people's biggest gain in past nine years of his government.
